clue.text: One of twelve on the board, maybe? should purge the system (12. 2 words)

definitions.text: One of twelve on the board, maybe?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dark piece in draughts (checkers), each player starting with twelve
second meaning: an old purgative medicine of senna and Epsom salts

explanation.surface: A player muses about one piece among twelve before deciding something must be flushed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; the dark pieces are one side's twelve men. The second half describes the remedy rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a dark checkers piece and a traditional laxative dose, so each half points at the same two words.

clue.text: British wine, seasoned brew

parts.note: standard abbreviation for British
rosé, the pink wine

explanation.surface: A British wine described as a well-seasoned brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Brose is a Scottish dish of oatmeal stirred with boiling water or stock and seasoned, a kind of savoury brew.

clue.text: Spun pulu found in flax, yielding sedative

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: line is the finer fibre of flax

indicators.note: fibre that is spun is twisted round, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: pulu is a silky fibre from Hawaiian tree ferns

explanation.surface: Twisted fern fibre mixed into flax produces a calming drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Line is a dictionary sense of flax fibre; the shuffled pulu sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupuline (lupulin) is the bitter powder from hop flowers, used medicinally as a mild sedative.

clue.text: Old Scottish porter judge preferred to English

indicators.note: preferred to can mean put forward ahead of, so one piece comes before the other

parts.note: a cadi is a judge in a Muslim country
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A judge is chosen over an English candidate in some old Scottish appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preferred' looks like choosing one over another; here it means placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadie or caddie was formerly a Scottish errand-runner or street porter, the source of the golfing word.

clue.text: Non-religious believer avoiding our circuitous path round lives

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the shortened word wraps the other piece
avoiding means steering clear of, so those letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: a detour is a roundabout route
taken as written, and removed
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A believer outside organised religion takes a winding path that skips our route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-religious' is fair because a deist accepts God but rejects organised, revealed religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A deist believes in a creator God through reason alone, rejecting revealed religion and its institutions.

clue.text: Wry humour I dropped describing unappealing old woman

indicators.note: a letter that is dropped falls away, so it is removed from the word before it

parts.note: irony is dry, wry humour
taken as written, and removed
on in the sense of about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone abandons dry wit while portraying an unattractive crone.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Shakespeare's: 'Aroint thee, witch! the rump-fed ronyon cries' in Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronyon is an archaic term of contempt for a mangy or scabby woman, so an unattractive old woman.

clue.text: A ragu cooked with a container with chef's coating (8, two words)

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed, so these letters are mixed into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A meat sauce is cooked in a tin and given a chef's topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish covered with breadcrumbs or grated cheese and browned, a coating chefs apply.

clue.text: How visitors behaved, stew being ruined in appearance

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dinner guests react politely to a stew that looks spoilt.

clue.text: Mouldy old tart woman scrapped

parts.note: tart as slang for a prostitute
standard abbreviation for woman, removed

explanation.surface: A stale old pastry gets binned along with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouldy old tart' reads as stale baking; 'old' marks the definition as an obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hore is an old spelling of hoar, which once meant grey with mould or musty.

clue.text: Mundane lapse in the midst of grief as of old

indicators.note: being in the midst of something means surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.definitionFit: Terrene means earthly or worldly, and mundane in its original sense is of this world.

clue.text: Like shrubby plant, as of old in a course sown wild

parts.note: taken as written
ut is Latin for as, the language of old

explanation.surface: Seed scattered over a course grows into something shrubby, in the old way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As of old' is the Latin word for as; it joins the letters of 'a course' before they are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutaceous means belonging to the rue family, Rutaceae, which includes shrubby plants such as rue and citrus.

clue.text: Personal article? Fool's beginning at the end

explanation.definitionFit: An op-ed is a newspaper opinion piece printed opposite the editorial page, voicing an individual's views.

clue.text: Keep on about repair, men needed

taken as written, and removed

explanation.definitionFit: Ding, chiefly Scots, means to insist or keep repeating, as in dinging on about something.

clue.text: Hamburger's additive often, rather rare in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle points to letters sitting inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A burger additive is cooked rather rare in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hamburger here is a person from Hamburg, not a burger; the additive is the title added to a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German courtesy title, added before a man's surname by a German such as someone from Hamburg.

clue.text: Like devout Muslim, endlessly, if such after conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes form, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A devout Muslim is described as endlessly so, if such a person has converted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufic means relating to Sufism, the mystical, devotional strand of Islam.

clue.text: Member of wind section hit seventh note in vivace

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for the tempo

parts.note: vivace is a lively, quick tempo marking
got in the sense of struck, as in 'got him on the chin'

explanation.surface: A wind player strikes the seventh note in a lively passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' in the sense of struck, as in 'the stone got him on the head'; vivace is an Italian tempo mark meaning lively and quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fagottist plays the fagotto, the Italian name for the bassoon, an orchestral woodwind instrument.

clue.text: After regular cutbacks armies rearm for a bit of a step up

clue.text: Reserve pedrero fired with entry of king

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suits a gun in the surface and also signals scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: To preorder something is to reserve it in advance, before it is available.

clue.text: Sandwich made with e.g. kipper involving oven

clue.text: Showing fossilized insect bits in mug, us included

taken as written

clue.text: Not a prima ballerina, have great fun dancing round fringe of Bolshoi

clue.text: Mercury in form of Fido's deity such as Dagon

indicators.note: in sets one piece inside the other's letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Dagon, the Philistine god, was traditionally depicted as half man and half fish, hence a god in fish form.

clue.text: People I see in flood of feeling demonstrating psychological breakdown

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for a surge

taken as written

clue.text: Writing I'm assigned to brought up what links religion and the law

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript
taken as written
on as in a task put on someone

explanation.definitionFit: To set foot in a place is to enter it, as a visitor does when dropping in.

clue.text: Opposed to going after tons? it's no longer worthwhile

clue.text: Like old undyed cloth, say, in mostly pale or dull
